summary: A research building at 1700 4th St, opened 2005, home to QB3 (California Institute for Quantitative Biosciences) director's office and central administration, built as a hub for academia-biotech collaboration.

milestones.text: UC Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings certifies a CEQA EIR addendum and approves the design of the California Institute for Bioengineering, Biotechnology, and Quantitative Biomedical Research (QB3) Building at Mission Bay -- this building, per QB3's own use of Byers Hall as its headquarters

facts.value: Bohlin Cywinski Jackson (corroborated by a former project manager's own portfolio and an architecture-press article, not confirmed directly on a UCSF-owned page)
QB3 director's office and central administration; academia-biotech collaboration space

images.credit: Byers Hall (left) and Genentech Hall (right), UCSF Mission Bay campus; "UCSF Medical Center at Mission Bay," presentation to the UC Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings, September 2008, "Architectural Context" slide
images.license_note: Slide from the presentation attached to the UC Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings' September 2008 meeting item approving the UCSF Medical Center at Mission Bay -- a public governing board's meeting record. Read 2026-09-19.
images.caption: Byers Hall and Genentech Hall
images.appeal_note: Dusk campus shot showing Byers Hall's glass-and-stone facade at left next to Genentech Hall across a landscaped lawn, warmly lit and well composed even though Byers Hall itself takes up the smaller share of the frame.

images.credit: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Farm Service Agency, NAIP aerial imagery (2024 flight), via USDA's 'latest NAIP' image service
images.license_note: USDA's data.gov catalog record for NAIP imagery sets the license to the U.S. government public-domain label (usa.gov/publicdomain/label/1.0); the USDA FSA policies page says public-domain information may be freely distributed with credit requested ('U.S. Department of Agriculture, Farm Service Agency'). Read 2026-09-22.
images.caption: USDA NAIP aerial orthophoto (2024 flight), cropped to the Mission Bay project area and its immediate surroundings
images.appeal_note: A straight-down orthophoto rather than an oblique aerial, but Oracle Park and Chase Center are both clearly recognizable landmarks in the frame, giving anyone who knows the city an immediate fix on the neighborhood.

images.credit: Firstcultural (Alfred Twu), aerial view from a departing flight, via Wikimedia Commons; CC0; downscaled to 1600 px
images.license_note: Wikimedia Commons' license box on the file page confirms CC0 (public domain dedication) by Firstcultural (Alfred Twu). Read 2026-09-23.
images.caption: Aerial view of Mission Bay, Oracle Park and the Caltrain/King Street area from a departing flight
images.appeal_note: Oracle Park's diamond and Chase Center's dome (with its own logo) are both clearly identifiable landmarks in one colorful frame -- reads far better at card size than the flatter government orthophoto.

open_questions: Architect not confirmed on any UCSF-owned page; sourced only to a former project manager's own portfolio and an architecture-press article.
Exact opening month and square footage not found in any source checked.
No openly licensed image was found; none is hosted here.

Images: the only photograph found of Byers Hall is undated beyond appearing in a September 2008 UC Regents presentation slide (shared with its neighbor); its exact capture date isn't confirmed. No site plan or architectural rendering specific to this building was found in a public-record source.

2026-09-21 pass: the March 2002 Regents design-approval item names the project 'the QB3 Building at Mission Bay,' not 'Byers Hall' -- the identification rests on QB3's own description of Byers Hall as its home building, not a direct name match in the Regents record.

2026-09-23 pass: searched for a construction or development cost figure (the March 2002 Regents design-approval item itself, which covers only the EIR addendum and design, not budget; UC Regents financing/capital-improvement agenda archives for a separate QB3 budget item; general web search for a press-reported figure). No cost was found; unlike its neighbors (Genentech Hall, Rock Hall, Rutter Center), no earlier Regents budget item naming this project was located in this pass.
